   174	/- Planner strategy: lem:cech_computes_cohomology ·
   175	Assembly of the four Route-A ingredients:
   176	
   177	(a) `cechAugmented_to_acyclicResolutionInput` yields:
   178	    · `e : F ≅ (cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F).cycles 0`
   179	    · `hexact : ∀ n, (cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F).ExactAt (n+1)`
   180	
   181	(b) `cechTerm_pushforward_acyclic` provides the typeclass instance:
   182	    `[∀ p, (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).IsRightAcyclic ((cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F).X p)]`
   183	    (introduce with `haveI` for each `p`; or use `inferInstance` if the `∀ p` form is
   184	    synthesisable from a blanket instance).
   185	
   186	(c) `Functor.rightDerivedIsoOfAcyclicResolution` (AcyclicResolution.lean, fully proved) with
   187	    G = `Scheme.Modules.pushforward f`, K = `cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F`, A = F, gives:
   188	    `((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).rightDerived i).obj F
   189	      ≅ ((G.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj (cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F)).homology i`
   190	
   191	(d) `pushforward_mapHomologicalComplex_cechComplexOnX` rewrites the right-hand side to
   192	    `(CechComplex f 𝒰 F).homology i`.
   193	
   194	The final iso `(CechComplex f 𝒰 F).homology i ≅ higherDirectImage f i F` is the composite of
   195	(d).symm, (c).symm, noting `higherDirectImage f i F = ((pushforward f).rightDerived i).obj F`.
   196	Wrap in `Nonempty` via `⟨iso⟩`.
   197	
   198	Additive / PreservesFiniteLimits hypotheses on `pushforward f`: `Additive` is an instance;
   199	`PreservesFiniteLimits` is needed for `rightDerivedIsoOfAcyclicResolution` (via
   200	`PreservesFiniteLimits (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f)` — left-exact since it is a right adjoint
   201	via the global sections adjunction). -/
   202	/-- **The Čech complex computes the higher direct images** (Stacks Tag 02KE;
   203	blueprint `lem:cech_computes_cohomology`).
   204	
   205	Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a separated quasi-compact morphism with `X` and `S` both separated, `F` a
   206	quasi-coherent `O_X`-module, `𝒰` a finite affine open cover of `X` (with all cover opens affine,
   207	`h𝒰 : ∀ i, IsAffine (𝒰.X i)`, so all intersections are affine by `X.IsSeparated`), and `hres`
   208	threading `HasInjectiveResolutions` on each intersection subscheme.  Then for every `i ≥ 0`
   209	there is an isomorphism between the `i`-th cohomology of the relative Čech complex and the `i`-th
   210	higher direct image:
   211	```
   212	  (CechComplex f 𝒰 F).homology i ≅ R^i f_* F  =  higherDirectImage f i F.
   213	```
   214	This is the canonical statement of the Čech-to-derived-pushforward comparison, proved under the
   215	correct hypotheses `[X.IsSeparated] [S.IsSeparated]` and `h𝒰`. -/
   216	theorem cech_computes_higherDirectImage [HasInjectiveResolutions X.Modules]
   217	    (f : X ⟶ S) [QuasiCompact f] [IsSeparated f] [X.IsSeparated] [S.IsSeparated]
   218	    (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) [Finite 𝒰.I₀] (h𝒰 : ∀ i, IsAffine (𝒰.X i))
   219	    (F : X.Modules) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherent) (i : ℕ)
   220	    (hres : ∀ (n : ℕ) (σ : Fin (n + 1) → 𝒰.I₀),
   221	      HasInjectiveResolutions (Scheme.Opens.toScheme (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ)).Modules) :
   222	    Nonempty ((CechComplex f 𝒰 F).homology i ≅ higherDirectImage f i F) := by
   223	  -- (a) the resolution data extracted from the exactness of the augmented Čech complex
   224	  obtain ⟨e, hexact⟩ := cechAugmented_to_acyclicResolutionInput 𝒰 h𝒰 F hF
   225	  -- (b) termwise right-`f_*`-acyclicity of the Čech complex on `X` (black box from
   226	  -- `CechTermAcyclic.lean`)
   227	  haveI : ∀ n, (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).IsRightAcyclic ((cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F).X n) :=
   228	    fun n => cechTerm_pushforward_acyclic f 𝒰 h𝒰 F hF n (hres n)
   229	  -- (c) `f_*` is left exact: it is a right adjoint (of the module pullback)
   230	  haveI : PreservesLimits (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f) :=
   231	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f).rightAdjoint_preservesLimits
   232	  -- (d) assemble: P4 acyclic-resolution comparison, then rewrite `f_* C•` to the relative
   233	  -- Čech complex; `higherDirectImage f i F` is definitionally `((f_*).rightDerived i).obj F`.
   234	  exact ⟨(HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor S.Modules (ComplexShape.up ℕ) i).mapIso
   235	      (pushforward_mapHomologicalComplex_cechComplexOnX f 𝒰 F).symm ≪≫
   236	    ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).rightDerivedIsoOfAcyclicResolution
   237	      (cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F) F e hexact i).symm⟩

   144	/-- An object `J : 𝒜` is *right-`G`-acyclic* when every higher right-derived
   145	functor of `G` vanishes at `J`:
   146	```
   147	(Rᵏ⁺¹ G)(J) = 0   for all k : ℕ.
   148	```
   149	The index-shifted quantifier `k + 1` matches the statement of
   150	`Functor.isZero_rightDerived_obj_injective_succ` and avoids an inequality
   151	side-condition; it is equivalent to `(Rⁿ G)(J) = 0` for all `n ≥ 1`.
   152	
   153	Blueprint: `CategoryTheory.Functor.IsRightAcyclic` (`def:right_acyclic`).
   154	-/
   155	class Functor.IsRightAcyclic (G : 𝒜 ⥤ ℬ) [G.Additive] (J : 𝒜) : Prop where
   156	  vanish : ∀ k : ℕ, Limits.IsZero ((G.rightDerived (k + 1)).obj J)
   157	
   158	/-- Every injective object is right-`G`-acyclic.
   159	Follows immediately from `Functor.isZero_rightDerived_obj_injective_succ`. -/

   161	    (G : 𝒜 ⥤ ℬ) [G.Additive] (J : 𝒜) [Injective J] : Functor.IsRightAcyclic G J where
   162	  vanish k := Functor.isZero_rightDerived_obj_injective_succ G k J
   163	-- Note: `Functor.isZero_rightDerived_obj_injective_succ` returns
   164	-- `Limits.IsZero ((G.rightDerived (k+1)).obj J)`, matching the class field.

   212	/-- **Dimension shift, part (1), from a degreewise-split SES of injective resolutions.**
   213	Given a short exact sequence `0 → A → J → Z → 0` lifted (via the horseshoe) to a
   214	degreewise-split short exact sequence of injective resolutions
   215	`0 → I_A → I_J → I_Z → 0`, presented here as chain maps `φ, ψ` with degreewise splittings,
   216	and with the middle object `J` right-`G`-acyclic, the connecting map of the homology long

   218	`(R^{k+1} G)(Z) ≅ (R^{k+2} G)(A)`.

   224	noncomputable def Functor.rightDerivedShiftIsoOfSplitResolutionSES

   226	    (I_A : InjectiveResolution A) (I_J : InjectiveResolution J) (I_Z : InjectiveResolution Z)

   230	    (splits : ∀ n, ((ShortComplex.mk φ ψ w).map

   235	      (G.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ))).ShortExact :=

   239	      (G.isZero_homology_mapHomologicalComplex_of_isRightAcyclic I_J k)
   240	      (G.isZero_homology_mapHomologicalComplex_of_isRightAcyclic I_J (k + 1)) ≪≫
   241	    (I_A.isoRightDerivedObj G (k + 2)).symm

   244	/-- **Horseshoe per-stage monomorphism.** Given an exact short complex
   245	`A → B → C` with `A → B` a monomorphism, and monomorphisms `α : A ↪ P`, `γ : C ↪ Q` with `P`

   250	`P = I_A.X (n+1)`, `Q = I_C.X (n+1)`, it produces the monomorphism into the next biproduct term
   251	whose cokernel feeds the following stage. -/
   252	lemma mono_biprod_lift_factorThru_of_exact {S : ShortComplex 𝒜} (hS : S.Exact) [Mono S.f]
   253	    {P Q : 𝒜} [Injective P] (α : S.X₁ ⟶ P) [Mono α] (γ : S.X₃ ⟶ Q) [Mono γ] :
   254	    Mono (biprod.lift (Injective.factorThru α S.f) (S.g ≫ γ)) := by
   255	  rw [Preadditive.mono_iff_cancel_zero]
   256	  intro T x hx
   257	  have h1 : x ≫ Injective.factorThru α S.f = 0 := by simpa using hx =≫ biprod.fst
   258	  have h2 : x ≫ S.g ≫ γ = 0 := by simpa using hx =≫ biprod.snd
   259	  have hxg : x ≫ S.g = 0 := by rw [← cancel_mono γ, zero_comp, Category.assoc]; exact h2
   260	  have hyf : hS.lift x hxg ≫ S.f = x := hS.lift_f x hxg
   261	  have hya : hS.lift x hxg ≫ α = 0 := by
   262	    have h3 : hS.lift x hxg ≫ S.f ≫ Injective.factorThru α S.f = 0 := by
   263	      rw [← Category.assoc, hyf]; exact h1
   264	    rwa [Injective.comp_factorThru] at h3
   265	  have hy0 : hS.lift x hxg = 0 := by rw [← cancel_mono α, zero_comp]; exact hya

   268	/-! ## Project-local Mathlib supplement — twisted biproduct of cochain complexes
   269	
   270	This block builds the *structural* core of the dual Horseshoe Lemma as a general, injective-free
   271	construction. Given two cochain complexes `K`, `L` and a degreewise family
   272	`τ n : L.X n ⟶ K.X (n+1)` satisfying the cocycle identity
   273	`L.d n (n+1) ≫ τ (n+1) = -(τ n ≫ K.d (n+1) (n+2))`, the biproduct objects `K.X n ⊞ L.X n` with the
   274	twisted matrix differential `[[d_K, τ], [0, d_L]]` form a cochain complex `twistedBiprod τ hτ`,
   275	the coprojection `K ⟶ twistedBiprod` and projection `twistedBiprod ⟶ L` are chain maps, and every
   276	degree is the canonical split short exact sequence of the biproduct.
   277	
   278	This is exactly the content of the blueprint sub-lemmas `lem:horseshoe_dComp` (the differential
   279	squares to zero) and `lem:horseshoe_chainMap` (the coprojection/projection are chain maps and the
   280	degrees split); it is isolated here free of injectivity because the only inputs are the cocycle
   281	identity and the biproduct structure. The horseshoe specialises it to `K = I_A.cocomplex`,
   282	`L = I_C.cocomplex` once the twist `τ` has been produced by injectivity. -/

   291	`K.X n ⊞ L.X n ⟶ K.X (n+1) ⊞ L.X (n+1)`. -/
   292	noncomputable def twistedBiprodD (n : ℕ) :
   293	    (K.X n ⊞ L.X n) ⟶ (K.X (n + 1) ⊞ L.X (n + 1)) :=
   294	  biprod.lift (biprod.fst ≫ K.d n (n + 1) + biprod.snd ≫ τ n) (biprod.snd ≫ L.d n (n + 1))
   295	
   296	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
   297	lemma twistedBiprodD_fst (n : ℕ) :
   298	    twistedBiprodD τ n ≫ biprod.fst = biprod.fst ≫ K.d n (n + 1) + biprod.snd ≫ τ n := by
   299	  simp [twistedBiprodD]
   300	
   301	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
   302	lemma twistedBiprodD_snd (n : ℕ) :
   303	    twistedBiprodD τ n ≫ biprod.snd = biprod.snd ≫ L.d n (n + 1) := by
   304	  simp [twistedBiprodD]

   311	  apply biprod.hom_ext
   312	  · simp only [Category.assoc, twistedBiprodD_fst, Preadditive.comp_add,
   313	      twistedBiprodD_fst_assoc, twistedBiprodD_snd_assoc, zero_comp]
   314	    rw [Preadditive.add_comp, Category.assoc, Category.assoc, HomologicalComplex.d_comp_d,
   315	      comp_zero, zero_add, ← Preadditive.comp_add, hτ n, add_neg_cancel, comp_zero]
   316	  · simp only [Category.assoc, twistedBiprodD_snd, twistedBiprodD_snd_assoc, zero_comp]

615	/-! ## Project-local Mathlib supplement — the augmented Čech complex on `X`
   616	
   617	The lemma `cechAugmented_exact` (`lem:cech_augmented_resolution`) asserts that the
   618	augmented {\v C}ech complex `0 → F → C⁰ → C¹ → ⋯` of a quasi-coherent sheaf `F`
   619	over an affine open cover `𝒰` is **exact** in `QCoh(X)` — i.e. the {\v C}ech nerve
   620	is a resolution of `F`. This is the *un-pushed* (over `X`, not relative to `f`)
   621	counterpart of `CechComplex`/`relativeCechComplexOfNerve`. We record here the
   622	structural ingredients that the exactness statement is phrased against: the
   623	un-augmented {\v C}ech complex on `X` (`cechComplexOnX`), obtained from the {\v C}ech
   624	nerve exactly as `relativeCechComplexOfNerve` does but with the *identity*
   625	pushforward — i.e. directly, with no `f_*`. -/
   626	
   627	/-- **The (un-augmented) {\v C}ech cochain complex of `F` on `X`.** This is the
   628	alternating-coface-map complex `C⁰ → C¹ → ⋯` of the underlying cosimplicial object
   629	of the {\v C}ech nerve `CechNerve 𝒰 F` (its augmentation `F` is dropped). It is the
   630	`f = 𝟙`/un-pushed analogue of `relativeCechComplexOfNerve`: the same coherence-free
   631	plumbing without the relative pushforward `f_*`, so it is the complex whose
   632	exactness (after re-adjoining the augmentation `F → C⁰`) is the content of
   633	`cechAugmented_exact`. Project-local. -/
   634	noncomputable def cechComplexOnX (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) (F : X.Modules) :
   635	    CochainComplex X.Modules ℕ :=
   636	  (AlgebraicTopology.alternatingCofaceMapComplex X.Modules).obj
   637	    (CosimplicialObject.Augmented.drop.obj (CechNerve 𝒰 F))
   638	
   639	/-- **The augmentation point of the {\v C}ech nerve is `F`.** The augmentation
   640	object `(CechNerve 𝒰 F).left` of the {\v C}ech nerve is `(𝟙 X)_* (𝟙 X)^* F` (the

 11516	\begin{proof}
 11517	  \uses{def:cech_complex_on_X, def:cech_complex}
 11518	  The direct image \(f_*\) is an additive functor, so it commutes with the functor
 11519	  that assembles a cosimplicial module into its alternating-coface cochain complex.
 11520	  Concretely, in each degree \(p\) both complexes have the same object, the image
 11521	  \(f_*(\mathcal{C}^p)\) of the degree-\(p\) {\v C}ech term; the degree-\(p\)
 11522	  differential of the relative {\v C}ech complex is exactly the image under \(f_*\) of
 11523	  the degree-\(p\) differential of the complex on \(X\). The latter differential is
 11524	  the alternating sum \(\sum_{j} (-1)^j \delta_j\) of the cofaces \(\delta_j\), and
 11525	  additivity of \(f_*\) --- its preservation of finite sums, of integer scalar
 11526	  multiples and of negation --- gives
 11527	  \[
 11528	    f_*\Bigl(\sum_j (-1)^j \delta_j\Bigr)
 11529	      \;=\;
 11530	    \sum_j (-1)^j\, f_*(\delta_j).
 11531	  \]
 11532	  Assembling these degreewise data --- the identity on objects together with the
 11533	  commuting squares expressing the differential identities --- produces the asserted
 11534	  isomorphism of cochain complexes.
 11535	\end{proof}

text: I’m making the first Lean edit in the abstract homological-algebra module: two reusable facts extract positive-degree exactness and the degree-zero cycles isomorphism from any exact augmentation, and a new derived-functor comparison consumes that exact augmentation directly. The generic proofs themselves elaborate; the first LSP pass found only namespace projection errors in the wrapper and an unused inherited injective-resolution instance. I’m qualifying the helper calls explicitly and scoping out that irrelevant instance, which keeps the API genuinely more general.
